item_identification.method: The leaf's old text names the effect 'Time Stop'. Enumerated every cached item whose text mentions stasis: data/items.json ids 2420 (Seeker's Armguard, EPIC), 3026 (Guardian Angel, revive-stasis, effect named Rebirth), 3157 (Zhonya's Hourglass, LEGENDARY), 228002 (Wooglet's Witchcap, DISTRIBUTED/non-SR-purchasable tier).
item_identification.conclusion: The coverage entry is the Time Stop item — Zhonya's Hourglass (3157) for a legendary Syndra loadout; Seeker's Armguard (2420) is its component and carries the identical Time Stop active. Both readings give the same answer below, because both items pair Time Stop with ability power.
item_identification.caveat: The scenario definition itself lives outside the permitted evidence tree (not present in data/practice-corpus/scenarios.json, which holds 22 non-Syndra scenarios), so the index->item binding is inferred from the old leaf text rather than read.

step_1_what_the_cached_wiki_text_says.quote: Put yourself in {{tip|stasis (buff)|stasis}} for {{fd|2.5}} seconds, rendering you {{tip|untargetable}} and {{tip|invulnerable}} for the duration but also unable to move, declare [[basic attack]]s, cast [[champion ability|abilities]], use [[summoner spell]]s, or [[active ability items|activate items]].
step_1_what_the_cached_wiki_text_says.reading: Time Stop is an ACTIVE with a fixed, bounded duration of 2.5 s. Nothing in the item text applies it passively: holding the item produces no stasis until it is used. Its effect is two-sided — it removes incoming damage (untargetable + invulnerable) AND it removes the holder's own ability to act for the same bounded interval.

step_2_declared_families_on_the_item.source_a: data/item-atoms/3157.json — declared atoms: stats.ability-power (family 'stats', flat 105.0), stats.armor (family 'stats', flat 50.0), crowd-control-mobility.stasis (family 'crowd-control-mobility', behavior 'Time Stop'), damage.resistance-mitigation (family 'damage', behavior 'Time Stop').
step_2_declared_families_on_the_item.source_b: data/atoms/items.json (unified atomizer, the current consumer per data/atoms/README.md) — objects['3157']: control.stasis [2.5 flat], damage.basic_attack (evidence 'active:Time Stop@kw:basic attack'), economy.total [3250 gold], stat.ability_power [105 flat], stat.armor [50 flat].
step_2_declared_families_on_the_item.source_c: data/item-atoms/2420.json (Seeker's Armguard) — same four families: stats.ability-power 40.0, stats.armor 25.0, crowd-control-mobility.stasis, damage.resistance-mitigation.
step_2_declared_families_on_the_item.family_vocabulary: data/wiki-atoms/ defines the family set actually in use: damage, crowd-control-mobility, heal-shield, interaction, stack-transform-summon-resource, vision-economy (+ 'stats'/'economy' structured blocks). There is no 'defence' family; 'damage' is defined in data/wiki-atoms/damage.json as 'A discrete offensive interaction that deducts a unit's current health' for damage.damage-instance.
step_2_declared_families_on_the_item.finding: The item's declared families are NOT all defensive. The 'stats' family carries 105 flat ability power (50 armor is the defensive half), and a 'damage'-family atom is declared on both tracked atom files. 105 AP is the reason an AP champion such as Syndra buys the item at all, and it raises outgoing damage directly. The new value's leading clause — 'Every declared family on this item is a defence' — is contradicted by data/items.json, data/item-atoms/3157.json and data/atoms/items.json.

step_3_does_the_mechanic_change_outgoing.formula_source: docs/math-foundations.md Section 1.1 (Renewal theory for cast + auto timing schedules)
step_3_does_the_mechanic_change_outgoing.quote_1: swings land at `0, Δ, 2Δ, …` with `Δ = 1/(AS · u)` where `AS` is total attack speed and `u` is the auto-attack uptime fraction
step_3_does_the_mechanic_change_outgoing.quote_3: Ability recasts are scheduled on **one shared timeline** (the champion has one set of hands): each cast occupies its sourced cast time, an ability recasts when its effective cooldown has elapsed *and* no other cast is in progress, and a cast counts when it *starts* within the window
step_3_does_the_mechanic_change_outgoing.argument: Totals are finite-horizon functionals of the acting window T. The cached wiki text says the holder is 'unable to move, declare basic attacks, cast abilities, use summoner spells, or activate items' for the stasis duration, so declaring s seconds of stasis inside a window T removes s seconds from the shared acting timeline: N drops from ⌊AS·u·T⌋ to ⌊AS·u·(T−s)⌋, and every ability cast that would have started in those seconds is displaced.

numbers.source_of_2.5: data/atoms/items.json objects['3157'] control.stasis values [2.5]; matches the {{fd|2.5}} in the wiki branch text

step_3_does_the_mechanic_change_outgoing.finding: The change in outgoing TDD is strictly non-zero for every realistic AS·u once stasis seconds are declared — about 4.2% of the acting window at T=60, i.e. 1–3 auto swings plus displaced casts. So the new value's second clause, 'the represented mechanic changes durability, not outgoing TDD', is quantitatively false: stasis changes outgoing TDD (downward). What is true is only the weaker statement that it never *increases* it.

step_4_check_the_old_value_against_the_s.claim_a: 'Time Stop is priced only from the explicit bounded active-seconds scenario input' — consistent: the duration is bounded and fixed at 2.5 s per activation in the cached data, and how many of those seconds fall inside the fight window (and against what incoming damage) is not derivable from the item record, so it must come from a scenario input.
step_4_check_the_old_value_against_the_s.claim_b: 'item presence alone never assumes stasis' — consistent: data/items.json places Time Stop under `active`, not `passives` ('Put yourself in stasis…'), so an unactivated Zhonya's contributes only its 105 AP / 50 armor stat block. Assuming stasis from mere presence would be an unsourced uptime assumption, and it is the same fail-closed posture the cached data forces elsewhere.
step_4_check_the_old_value_against_the_s.finding: Both clauses of the old value are supported by the cached item record; neither is contradicted by anything in data/ or docs/math-foundations.md.

conclusion: The new value fails on both clauses. (1) 'Every declared family on this item is a defence' is contradicted by the item's own declared atoms: the stats family carries 105 flat ability power — an offensive stat, and the reason an AP champion buys the item — and a `damage`-family atom is declared in both the per-item and unified atom files. (2) 'the represented mechanic changes durability, not outgoing TDD' is contradicted by the cached wiki text ('unable to move, declare basic attacks, cast abilities…') combined with docs/math-foundations.md's N(T) = ⌊AS·u·T⌋: 2.5 declared stasis seconds in a 60 s window remove 4.17% of the acting timeline, costing 1–3 auto swings plus displaced casts. The old value states exactly the right thing for this item — a bounded (2.5 s) ACTIVE that is priced only from an explicit scenario input and is never assumed from possession.
